question: Should QQBot permanently reject inbound gateway frames above 1 MiB without a published QQ maximum, or should a different ceiling be established from provider or production evidence?
rationale: This threshold trades memory-exhaustion protection against delivery and connection availability for large valid events; repository inspection cannot determine the intended QQ protocol boundary.

options.title: Establish contract-backed ceiling
options.body: Use QQ documentation, SDK behavior, or redacted production-frame measurements to choose a defensible limit with explicit headroom.

options.title: Approve 1 MiB explicitly
options.body: A QQBot owner accepts the inferred envelope analysis and owns the delivery and reconnect risk of this fixed threshold.

recommendation.title: Establish contract-backed ceiling
recommendation.body: Use QQ documentation, SDK behavior, or redacted production-frame measurements to choose a defensible limit with explicit headroom.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged QQBot gateway architecture history makes this the strongest available owner for the channel-specific inbound protocol boundary.
